resources.string: Motile cilia on the ependymal lining of the brain ventricles can help move nearby cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). This model compares two repeating beats with the same invented frequency and a chosen timing offset. The intervals are fictional, not seconds. The model does not predict real beat rates or CSF flow and does not guide interventions.

Unwrapped phase difference (cycles) = toy frequency (cycles per interval) × timing offset (intervals). The wrapped value keeps only the fractional part, so every whole cycle returns to the same phase as zero offset.
